title: As a developer, I can define an agent with typed custom tools in a few lines of code
As an ai-native user, I can have a coding agent scaffold a new agent project from an official CLI or template in one command
As an ai-native user, I can rely on strict typing and schema validation so a coding agent catches its own mistakes at build time
As an ai-native user, I can run the framework's example agents headlessly from a terminal so an agent can verify what it just built
As a developer, I can orchestrate multiple agents — handoffs, subagents, or crews — inside one workflow
As a developer, I can compose agents into an explicit graph or workflow with branching, loops, and parallel steps
As a developer, I can checkpoint agent state so a run can resume exactly where it left off after a crash or restart
As an engineering-lead, I can run long-lived agents durably across process restarts and deploys, natively or via durable-execution integrations
As a developer, I can pause an agent mid-run for human input or approval and resume with the human's decision
As an engineering-lead, I can require human approval before specific sensitive tool calls execute
As a developer, I can stream tokens and intermediate agent events (tool calls, steps) to my UI in real time
As a developer, I can get schema-validated structured output from an agent, with automatic retries when validation fails
As a developer, I can give agents long-term memory that persists across sessions and threads
As a developer, I can trim, summarize, or filter conversation history to keep an agent inside its context window
As an engineering-lead, I can score agent quality with built-in evals and run them as part of CI
As a developer, I can trace every LLM call and tool invocation of an agent run in an observability UI
As a developer, I can unit-test agents with mocked models and tools
As an engineering-lead, I can deploy an agent to a managed runtime and call it as an API endpoint
As an engineering-lead, I can run my agents entirely on my own infrastructure with no dependence on the vendor's platform
As a developer, I can swap the underlying LLM provider or model without rewriting my agent
As a developer, I can attach input/output guardrails that validate, transform, or block unsafe content
As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution
